import numpy as np, json
meta = json.load(open('/work/tf12_meta.json'))
ids12 = np.load('/work/fwd_12/input_ids.npy'); lp12 = np.load('/work/fwd_12/token_logprobs.npy')
tk = np.load('/work/fwd_12/topk_ids.npy', mmap_mode='r')
assert all(list(ids12[i, :3]) == meta[i][5] for i in range(len(meta)))
R = {}
for i, (F, pid, st, n, spans, _) in enumerate(meta):
    body = lp12[i, st-1:n-1].astype(np.float64)
    cat = {'copied': [], 'new': []}; hit = {'copied': [], 'new': []}
    for ti, c in spans:
        cat[c].append(lp12[i, ti-1]); hit[c].append(int(tk[i, ti-1, 0] == ids12[i, ti]))
    R.setdefault(pid, {})[F] = (body.mean(), np.mean(cat['copied']) if cat['copied'] else np.nan, np.mean(cat['new']) if cat['new'] else np.nan,
                                np.mean(hit['copied']) if hit['copied'] else np.nan, np.mean(hit['new']) if hit['new'] else np.nan)
names = ['body lp', 'copied lp', 'new lp', 'copied top1', 'new top1']
P = list(R)
for k, nm in enumerate(names):
    a = np.array([R[p]['F1'][k] for p in P]); b = np.array([R[p]['F2'][k] for p in P]); ok = ~np.isnan(a) & ~np.isnan(b)
    d = b[ok] - a[ok]
    print(f"{nm:12s} chat F1 {np.nanmean(a):+.3f} | raw F2 {np.nanmean(b):+.3f} | paired F2-F1 {d.mean():+.4f} +- {d.std(ddof=1)/np.sqrt(ok.sum()):.4f} (n {ok.sum()})")

No hidden pass/fail decision exists at the end of the prompt. A correct-minus-wrong direction separates the outcomes on held-out problems with AUC 0.66–0.72 at every layer. That is already 0.68 at layer 1, where almost no computation has happened, and equal to what the number of solution steps alone gives (0.68). The projection also tracks step count closely (r ≈ −0.3 to −0.5). So the prompt state only encodes difficulty and length, as in any natural model, and this line is closed.

The remaining question is whether this model can do better at all. Every check says the weights and computations look natural, so the question is whether the capability is latent (suppressed in the chat/evaluation context) or simply absent. A suppression mechanism keyed to the chat persona would leave the same weights reasoning better in a different context.

I will teacher-force the same reference solutions, with the GSM8K calculator annotations stripped, in two formats:
- the evaluation chat prompt;
- a raw pre-training-style "Question: …\nAnswer: …" text with no chat template.

I then compare the log-probability of the critical tokens, the choice of which quantity from the problem to use next and the first digit of computed results. Much better critical-token prediction in raw format would mean the chat/IT context suppresses an existing capability, and the chat-vs-raw contrast becomes a lead to trace. Equal or worse would mean the weakness is intrinsic.

First I need the exact evaluation prompt format.

The evaluation prompt is the Gemma chat template with the problem followed by the fixed instruction. I now build the teacher-forcing texts for 500 DEV problems (DEV[512:1012]), not used in my generation passes so far. I strip the GSM8K calculator annotations from each reference solution so it reads naturally, keeping the final "#### answer" line. Each cleaned solution goes in two formats:
- **F1:** the exact evaluation chat prompt;
- **F2:** a raw "Question: …\nAnswer: " text with only BOS.

I mark the first token of every number in the solution body and classify it as either:
- **copied:** the number appears in the problem, so this is a choice of which quantity to use;
- **new:** a computed result.

I verify that my tokenization reproduces the tool's token ids. The pass then returns token log-probabilities and the top-5 predictions. The decisive comparison is critical-token log-probability, paired by problem, raw versus chat.

The texts are built: 1,000 in total (500 DEV problems × 2 formats), 171k tokens, at most 377 per text. On average each has about 13 marked number positions, 41% of them quantities copied from the problem. Both formats start with BOS (id 2), so the template tokens are parsed as special tokens. I run the teacher-forced pass on the original weights (no edit is saved), returning token log-probabilities and the top-5 predictions.
